House Bill 4002 gives individuals caught with substances like fentanyl, heroin or meth the option to face a misdemeanor charge or to enter a treatment pathway that includes a behavioral‑health program and a deflection initiative designed to avoid fines. Possession for personal use would be punishable by up to six months in jail."

Supporters argue this flexibility lets each region tailor solutions to its resources, whereas critics warn it could produce a confusing and unequal patchwork of rules."
